content: Yes, the concerns you raise—long‑lived radioactive waste, the high upfront and ongoing costs of building and decommissioning nuclear facilities, and the relatively speculative risk of a few blackouts that renewables (solar, wind, hydro) can largely offset—are the core objections many people cite when voting to keep the ban. While the debate remains nuanced (some see nuclear as a low‑carbon baseload source that could complement intermittent renewables), the weight of waste, financial burden, and safety considerations makes the “no nuclear” position a compelling stance for many voters.
